standard_prerequisites: ordinal addition defined via the lexicographic order type of a two-piece concatenation
strict suprema of sets of ordinals
initial segments of ordinal order types
core_obligations: Verify the three recursion equations for ordinal addition: alpha+0=alpha, alpha+(beta+1)=(alpha+beta)+1, and alpha+beta = strict sup over delta<beta of (alpha+delta) when beta is a limit ordinal
proof_roadmap: Base case: compute the order type of the concatenation with an empty second piece and read off alpha
Successor case: the second piece of the concatenation for beta+1 is a singleton block, which shifts the order type by one, giving (alpha+beta)+1
Limit case: if beta is a limit, each delta<beta has delta+1<beta, so alpha+delta is a proper initial segment of alpha+beta, making alpha+beta a strict upper bound of the set of partial sums
Conversely every ordinal gamma with alpha <= gamma < alpha+beta equals some alpha+delta with delta<beta, so alpha+beta is exactly the strict supremum
difficulty_reason: Straightforward case-by-case verification from the order-type definition of addition; the limit case needs the initial-segment observation, which the source spells out.
